claim_verdicts.evidence: ASP.NET Core 10.0 logging page: "The logging libraries implicitly create a scope object with ActivityTrackingOptions. The following fields indicate the options: SpanId, TraceId, ParentId, Baggage, Tags. SpanId, TraceId, ParentId are enabled by default." Execution: outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/json-logs.txt lines 19-25 show a Scopes entry with SpanId, TraceId, ParentId.

ASP.NET Core logging page: "If a provider supports log scopes, IncludeScopes indicates whether they're enabled." Console log formatting page shows Json formatter configured via Logging:Console:FormatterOptions:IncludeScopes. Execution: outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/json-logs.txt lines 19-35 show "Scopes": [ {"Message": "SpanId:..., TraceId:..., ParentId:...", "SpanId": ..., "TraceId": ..., "ParentId": ...}, ... ].

docker-compose.yml: api line 194, notifications 326, payments 387, fake-gateway 417 set Logging__Console__FormatterOptions__IncludeScopes: "true" next to Logging__Console__FormatterName: "json" (180, 322, 383, 413); comment at 191-193: "Only this setting changed, no log call." Read from the submodule working tree (images tagged :stage-3); `git show stage-3:docker-compose.yml` was blocked by the permission system in round 1.

RequestLoggingMiddleware.cs lines 17-22: logger.LogInformation("{Method} {Path} responded {StatusCode} in {ElapsedMs}ms", Method, Path, StatusCode, ElapsedMilliseconds). outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/json-logs.txt: Category DonHang.Api.Middleware.RequestLoggingMiddleware with Scopes entry SpanId/TraceId/ParentId. Round 2: git ls-tree stage-3 lists DonHang.Api/Middleware/RequestLoggingMiddleware.cs, matching the new gloss.

Alloy loki.process: stage.json "parses incoming log lines ... as JSON and uses JMESPath expressions to extract new values"; stage.structured_metadata "can read data from the extracted values map and add them to log entries as structured metadata"; "If the value is empty, it's inferred to be the same as the key." Execution: logs-for-trace.txt returns lines matched by trace_id="...", so the expression yields the TraceId.

Claim restated as a fact about the config comment. git show stage-3:deploy/monitoring/alloy/config.alloy line 33: "// stream for every request. A line with no trace id passes through as it is...". The lesson (section 5) and quiz q7 now attribute the pass-through to this comment, not to Alloy's documentation. The underlying Alloy behaviour stays undocumented (round 1 fetch), which the lesson no longer asserts.

Loki structured metadata page: structured metadata is "a way to attach metadata to logs without indexing them"; recommended for "high cardinality metadata that should not be used as a label and does not exist in the log line". The page uses trace_id as its example of structured metadata.

Loki labels page: "If another unique combination of labels comes in (for example, status_code=\"500\") another new stream is created." "In Loki, the content of each log line is not indexed." "Imagine now if you set a label for ip. Not only does every request from a user become a unique stream." "High cardinality causes Loki to build a huge index..."

Log queries page: "!=: Log line does not contain string"; "Label filter expression allows filtering log line using their original and extracted labels." Structured metadata page (round 2 fetch): "You can use labels of structured metadata to filter log line using a label filter expression." Example {job="example"} | pod="myservice-abc1234-56789".

git show stage-3:scripts/backend/logs-for-trace.sh: line 23 id=$(trace_id "$traceparent"); line 30 query="{service=~\"api|payments|notifications\"} | trace_id=\"$id\" != \"Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore\" != \"System.Net.Http\""; lines 25-31 match the lesson block character for character.

Only a start time is sent, as the revised section 5 now says.

outputs/stage-3/scripts/backend/logs-for-trace.txt lines 1-7 equal the lesson's output block: "-> 202", the logql> line, then api POST ... responded 202, notifications refund requested email, payments Refund ... done, notifications order refunded email.

datasources.yml lines 25-32: derivedFields: - name: TraceId, matcherType: label, matcherRegex: trace_id, datasourceUid: tempo, url: "$${__value.raw}", urlDisplayLabel: "Open the trace"; Tempo data source uid: tempo (line 38). Read from the submodule working tree; git show at the tag was blocked in round 1.

Claim now uses round-1 suggested_text. Grafana Loki configure page: "When the type is Label, the input matches as a regular expression against label keys"; Internal link: "Toggle on to define an internal link to a tracing data source." Loki structured metadata page (round 2 fetch): "Structured metadata is extracted automatically for each returned log line and added to the labels returned for the query." This closes the round-1 inference gap.

Prometheus data model: "Every time series is uniquely identified by its metric name and optional key-value pairs called labels." "The change of any label's value, including adding or removing labels, will create a new time series." Round 2, zero issues: re-read changed sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and quiz q7; opened Loki structured-metadata page, config.alloy and scripts/backend/trace-refund.sh @ stage-3.

issues.text: New in round 2. I had to read this paragraph twice. Section 4 told me trace_id is not a label, and here a derived field 'of type Label' matches 'a label key', with the reason tucked into a parenthesis. 'internal link' and 'target data source' also arrive as Grafana settings I have not seen. I follow it on the second pass, but it is the densest paragraph in the lesson.
issues.quote: In Grafana's Loki data source, a derived field of type Label matches a label key of each line (Loki returns structured metadata among a line's labels)
issues.fix: Split it: first one sentence 'When Loki returns a line, it lists the line's structured metadata together with its labels, so Grafana can match `trace_id` the same way as a label.', then the derived-field sentence without the parenthesis.
